open.speaker: walt
lines: ...You're them Sutton people. Marlene said you'd be round. Said you listen. We'll see.

passives.line: The run's been patched at the top of the wire, not the bottom. Whatever got in came over, not under, and it came over eight feet.
He wants you off his step. His boots say he wants somebody on it. Stay where you are, and don't shift your weight.
Porch light's on at noon. He has not turned it off since Thursday. He has not slept since Thursday either.

options.text: We heard you lost a hen.
Porch light's doing a lot of work for noon.
That patch is at the top of the wire. Something came over, not under.
Those Dominiques? Good layers in the cold.
(Stand on the step and say nothing.)

hen.speaker: walt
lines: Lost three. Lost a dog in '87 the same way, and nobody come round then neither, so don't act like you're doing me a favour.
Didn't eat 'em. That's what I can't get past. Took 'em over the wire and left 'em in the ditch by the road, not a mark on 'em. What takes a hen and don't eat it.
Nothing that's hungry. Something that's angry, or something that's playing.

light.speaker: walt
lines: ...It don't like the light. Thursday it come to the edge of the yard and stopped where the light stopped. I know that much, and that's more than the deputy knows.
Stopped at the edge of the light. Walt, did the light flicker? Did it dim?
...Went brown. Like when the well pump kicks in. Then it was gone.

over.speaker: walt
lines: ...Yeah. Eight foot of wire, and it come over with a hen in its mouth and never touched the top. I'd have heard the wire sing.
You can look. Nobody else bothered to look, they just stood on my step and said coyote.
Eight feet with a load and no contact. That's not a jump. That's something coming down from higher.

over_fail.speaker: walt
lines: Coons. Patch is where the coons go, same as any farm. You ever kept a bird in your life?
You want fur on a fence, go to the church lot. Reverend's got some on his wire too, and he ain't a farmer, so he'll think it's special.

layers.speaker: walt
lines: Barred Rocks. But close enough that you've been near a coop, which is more than the last three.
Since I was six. Fort Campbell woods.
Huh. Then you know what an owl looks like by flashlight, and you know this wasn't one.

layers_fail.speaker: walt
lines: Don't talk chickens at me like you know chickens. Them's Barred Rocks and you'd know it if you'd ever stood in a coop.
City. Every one of you. Marlene said you listened. She didn't say you knew anything.

silent.speaker: walt
lines: Well. You ain't talked yet. That's more than the deputy managed, and he had a hat on.
Wipe your feet if you're coming in. Coffee's burnt.

hub.speaker: walt
lines: Say it or don't. I got birds to feed, what's left of 'em.

options.text: We're not leaving till we've seen the fence.
We'll leave you to your birds.

gun.speaker: walt
lines: (He reaches behind the door and comes back with a shotgun. He does not point it. He does not need to.)
Walt. Nobody here is armed and nobody here is from the county. Put it down and we'll talk or we'll go.

passives.line: Breech is open. It's not loaded, or he wants you to think it's not. Either way: feet planted, hands open, eyes on his, not on it.

stays.speaker: walt
lines: Hell. Hell, you're either stupid or you mean it.
(He breaks the gun over his arm. It was empty.) Come see the wire. Bag what's on it, I ain't touching it.
That's the Walt I'd have bet on.

stays_fail.speaker: walt
lines: Come back with a warrant or a backbone. Don't much care which.

backed_down.speaker: walt
lines: Smart. Marlene said you listened. Guess you do.
(He puts the gun back behind the door.) Fence is round the side. I didn't say you could look. I didn't say you couldn't.
That's as close to yes as he gets.
